The code is **IXGC**. It's hidden in the hidden-layer biases, `b1`, as letter codes.

**Where it is.** The last four entries of `b1`, for hidden units 28 to 31, are:

| Unit | b1 value | ×1000 | ASCII letter |
|---|---|---|---|
| 28 | 0.073 | 73 | I |
| 29 | 0.088 | 88 | X |
| 30 | 0.071 | 71 | G |
| 31 | 0.067 | 67 | C |

**Why I think this is the hidden code and not chance:**
- The other biases spread over about −0.45 to +0.65. A bias landing in the narrow 0.065–0.090 band that maps to a capital letter is rare. Four in a row at the very end of the list is very unlikely to happen by accident.
- Most of these units also stand out in the weights. Units 29, 30 and 31 (plus unit 27 next to them) are very clean "three in a row" detectors: right column, bottom row, the 2-4-6 diagonal, and the top row. That looks like the end of the layer was deliberately edited. Unit 28, the "I", is the exception, since its weights aren't clean.
- Because the values are so small, they barely change how the network plays. That fits a code hidden so it doesn't affect behaviour.

I didn't run any code, as you asked, so this came from reading the numbers. I also looked for letter shapes drawn on the 3×3 board in the weights and for other runs of letter-like values. Neither turned up a code.

CODE: IXGC
